newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: RUGBY UNION-SRI LANKA-SINGAPORE MATCH PUT OFF.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SRI LANKA-SINGAPORE MATCH PUT OFF.

text.p: The World Cup Rugby qualifier between Sri Lanka and Singapore scheduled for January 18 in Colombo has been postponed for security reasons, the manager of the Sri Lankan team said on Wednesday.

"Unfortunately Singapore has written to the World Cup Rugby Union saying there's been an escalation of violence in Sri Lanka and that for security reasons they can't come now," said Maiya Gunasekera, who is also vice president of the Sri Lanka Rugby Football Union.

"We wrote back asking for the match to be rescheduled for March 1," he told Reuters. "We also said whatever violence there is, (it is away) from Colombo and that sporadic violence is bound to take place right throughout the year. The city of Colombo is no less safer than London."

Security in Colombo has been tightened because of the threat of attacks by Tamil Tiger rebels who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.

The rebels last Thursday attacked army positions in northern Paranthan, 320 km (200 miles) from the capital Colombo, in a massive raid in which the government said 223 soldiers and 350 guerrillas were killed.

Last January, a rebel suicide bomber blew up the central bank in Colombo killing almost 100 people. In July, two briefcase bombs ripped through a crowded commuter train in a Colombo suburb killing nearly 60 people.
Gunasekera said the island's first match in the qualifying round will be against Thailand on February 15 in Thailand.
